text:
Pavel Buchnevich's last ten games read like a slump: two goals, zero assists, and our numbers expected about five and a half points from the minutes he played. Look underneath and most of the slump is on the scoresheet. The Blues take 54% of the expected goals at five-on-five with him on the ice (expected goals measure the quality of chances), about four points better than when he sits, and his own chances, worth 5.33 expected goals, outrun his four goals.

That reads like a playmaker whose linemates aren't finishing. He's a passer by habit: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 19% of his setups coming from behind the net last season, more than double a typical forward, the kind of feed that makes a goalie turn his head. The worry for St. Louis is that Evolving-Hockey rated his 2025-26 around replacement level.

At 31, with 506 career points before this season, he's projected by our numbers for around 41 this year. Watch the assists. If they come back, the process was fine all along.
headline: Buchnevich's slump lives on the scoresheet
